question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India have been adopted from the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Irish Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• DPSP

 
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy(Article 36 to 51).
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) of the Indian Constitution was influenced by a similar feature of the Irish Constitution. Hence, Option 4 is correct.
 
• Dr B R Ambedkar called DPSP "Novel features of the Indian constitution".
 
• K.T Shah called DPSP as "A cheque on a bank payable at the convenience of the bank".
 
• Directive Principles deal with economic, social, and cultural rights.
 
• Directive Principles are non-justiciable (Article 37).
 
• Sapru committee incorporated the Directive Principles of State Policy into the Indian constitution.
